newsitem.title: USA: Maine Turnpike Auth. seeks vote on road-widening.
newsitem.headline: Maine Turnpike Auth. seeks vote on road-widening.

text.p: The Maine Turnpike Authority on Tuesday agreed to ask the voters to approve a $58 million project to widen 36 miles of the toll road in the southern part of the state.

The referendum plan, which goes to the Legislature, would schedule a November election on whether to widen the 49-year-old highway to three lanes in each direction between the towns of York and Scarborough.
The authority was not required to ask for voter approval, but officials were concerned environmentalists would attempt to delay or block the project by gathering signatures to force a vote in 1998.

"While we're not required to do this. I think it is very prudent as a business decision to get the sign-off from everyone," Julian Coles, chairman of the authority, told reporters after the unanimous vote.

Environmentalists forced a similar referendum in 1991, and voters overwhelmingly blocked a move to widen the road. Opponents had argued that not enough effort had been made to create alternatives to automobile transportation.
A study last year concluded the road was already overloaded, and turnpike officials have maintained that alternative efforts to ease congestion would not be adequate during the summer tourist season.
Officials said if approved the project would likely increase toll rates by about four percent. The state-owned turnpike is entirely self-financed. ((--Boston bureau, 617-367-4106))
